records.name: Nicaragua
records.summary_text: Nicaragua is a country that demands real caution from trans visitors. Nothing criminalises being trans — sodomy was decriminalised in 2008 — but NGOs document 108 cases of violence against the LGBTIQ+ community in 2024 alone and 10 murders of trans women in the last two and a half years, and arbitrary detention is used broadly against perceived opponents. Since 2018 virtually all independent civil society has been shut down or exiled, so there is no domestic protection infrastructure and no recourse for a visitor facing harm.

records.name: Guyana
records.summary_text:
Guyana is dangerous for trans visitors — one of only five Western-Hemisphere countries still criminalising same-sex conduct (buggery carries life imprisonment on paper, though rarely enforced). The IACHR heard evidence in November 2024 of severe violence against trans women: 69 cases of violence against trans women documented 2018–2022, in a country of under a million people. Police fail to investigate anti-LGBT violence; there is no anti-discrimination legislation (the UN Human Rights Committee called for it in April 2024) and no legal gender recognition.
